result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure and discontinuous sidewalks in a residential setting. A wide, unmarked access road creates a significant conflict point for pedestrians walking along the main street.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Driveway Entrance
hazards.description: The entrance to the residential access road is wide and lacks markings, creating a large conflict zone where turning vehicles may not expect pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, where the sidewalk meets the access road.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks across the main road, forcing pedestrians to cross unprotected in an area with no traffic control.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side of the image terminates at the access road and does not clearly continue on the other side, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the access road entrance.

interventions.title: Raised Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Implement a raised sidewalk across the driveway entrance to maintain pedestrian priority and slow entering/exiting vehicles.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalk and Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalk markings and pedestrian crossing warning signs to designate a safe crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Radius Reduction
interventions.description: Tighten the curb radii at the access road entrance to reduce vehicle turning speeds and shorten the pedestrian crossing distance.
